wins: Mapped external attack surface fully within the allotted time, capturing service banners on 4 hosts.
Documented detailed vulnerability hypotheses supporting the reward 110 despite no compromise, enabling faster future exploitation planning.
fails: Failed to deliver successful privilege escalation due to persistent authentication blocks and missing credentials.
No post-exploitation persistence steps executed, halting progress beyond initial reconnaissance.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance succeeded with high fidelity, but execution stalled before exploitation/persistence, leaving reward limited to preparatory intelligence.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Authorization attempts using default credentials were repeatedly blocked by account lockouts when targeting SSH services.

skill_cards.if_condition: When discovering live hosts during nmap scans
skill_cards.then_action: Use nmap -sV --script=banner,vuln to capture service fingerprints and preliminary CVE data

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 returns SSH banner with supported authentication methods
skill_cards.then_action: Chain hydra brute-force with targeted username list before invoking enumeration

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH brute-force triggers lockout behavior
skill_cards.then_action: Shift to banner grabbing and OS fingerprinting to prepare alternative exploitation vectors

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in reconnaissance phase

next_experiments.title: Credential spray with timing controls
next_experiments.description: Implement targeted credential spray using a throttled hydra run and rotating IP to reduce lockouts and identify valid SSH credentials.

next_experiments.title: Pivot from SSH to HTTP exploits
next_experiments.description: After mapping services, focus on HTTP endpoints with nikto and OWASP Zap to find exploitable web vulnerabilities for initial foothold.

next_experiments.title: Post-compromise persistence plan
next_experiments.description: Draft scripted persistence routines (e.g., cron job via limited shell) ready to deploy immediately after any future successful access.
